# Golden traces for the legacy transcoders (kernel/src/legacy, kernel/src/lightningrod).
# Every row is a published example or a value worked out by hand below; none was produced
# by running the code under test. See bench/README.md, "Sources of the golden traces".
# Columns (tab separated): kind  input  arg  expected
#   comp3_dec   packed bytes (hex)        -            signed integer       cobol.c comp3_decode
#   comp3_enc   signed integer            nbytes       packed bytes (hex)   cobol.c comp3_encode
#   zoned_dec   EBCDIC zoned bytes (hex)  -            signed integer       cobol.c zoned_decode
#   zoned_enc   signed integer            ndigits,s|u  zoned bytes (hex)    cobol.c zoned_encode
#   comp_dec    big-endian bytes (hex)    s|u          signed integer       cobol.c comp_decode
#   comp_enc    signed integer            size,s|u     bytes (hex)          cobol.c comp_encode
#   lr_packed   packed bytes (hex)        scale        num/den (reduced)    lightningrod lr_packed_to_rat
#   lr_zoned    zoned bytes (hex)         scale        num/den (reduced)    lightningrod lr_zoned_to_rat
#   hfp32_ieee  IBM HFP single (hex)      -            IEEE binary32 (hex)  fortran.c hfp32_to_ieee32
#   ieee32_hfp  IEEE binary32 (hex)       -            IBM HFP single (hex) fortran.c ieee32_to_hfp32
#   hfp64_ieee  IBM HFP double (hex)      -            IEEE binary64 (hex)  fortran.c hfp64_to_ieee64
#   ieee64_hfp  IEEE binary64 (hex)       -            IBM HFP double (hex) fortran.c ieee64_to_hfp64
# [A] IBM Enterprise COBOL Programming Guide, "Examples of numeric data and internal
#     representation" (value 1234 / -1234 in DISPLAY, PACKED-DECIMAL and BINARY).
# [B] Worked by hand from the packed/zoned rules (two digits per byte, sign nibble C/D/F
#     last; zoned digit F0-F9, sign in the last byte's zone).
#     PIC S9(3) COMP-3 zero and minus one: 00 0C, 00 1D.
#     A value that does not fit: 1000 in 2 bytes (3 digits) must be refused.
#     Zoned with implied decimals, PIC S9(3)V99 -123.45 = F1 F2 F3 F4 D5 -> -12345/100 = -2469/20.
#     Signed overpunch of a last digit 0: +0 = C0 ("{"), -10 = F1 D0 ("1}").
# [C] IBM System/360 hexadecimal floating point. Single: sign bit, 7-bit excess-64 base-16
#     exponent, 24-bit fraction 0.f (hex). The -118.625 example (C276A000) is the one
#     given in the Wikipedia article "IBM hexadecimal floating-point"; the IEEE side is
#     Double: same exponent byte, 56-bit fraction. IEEE binary64 exponent 1023+6 = 0x405
